research_mode: official Environment Agency, Met Office and UK Health Security Agency primary sources only; flood warnings, flood-map planning, surface-water, severe-weather warning and weather-health alert methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Official severe-weather warning responsibility
verified_claims: The Met Office, as the UK's official weather service, issues warnings about impacts from severe weather.
limitations: A national warning service does not provide property-condition observations.

sources.name: Continuous warning operation
verified_claims: The Met Office warning operation runs 24 hours a day and 365 days a year.
limitations: Continuous operation does not mean a warning is active for every hazard or location.

sources.name: Warning forecast horizon
verified_claims: Warnings can be provided up to seven days ahead.
limitations: The maximum horizon does not imply equal certainty across all seven days.

sources.name: Warning hazard family
verified_claims: Warnings cover rain, thunderstorms, wind, snow, lightning, ice, extreme heat and fog.
limitations: The hazard list is not an exhaustive inventory of every local public-safety threat.

sources.name: Warning message structure
verified_claims: Warnings contain a headline, what to expect, what to do and further details.
limitations: Structured sections support interpretation but do not convert forecasts into observed impacts.

sources.name: Warning colour family
verified_claims: National Severe Weather Warning Service warnings use yellow, amber and red colours.
limitations: Colour must not be treated as a standalone numeric risk score.

sources.name: Impact-likelihood warning basis
verified_claims: Warning colour is determined from a combination of potential impact and likelihood.
limitations: Neither colour nor likelihood alone identifies exact impact at a particular parcel.

sources.name: Warning impact matrix
verified_claims: The warning's further details show an impact matrix with the selected impact-likelihood combination.
limitations: The matrix is a forecast communication tool and not an event verification record.

sources.name: Yellow-warning interpretation range
verified_claims: Yellow warnings can represent likely low-level impacts or lower-certainty scenarios with more severe potential impacts.
limitations: Yellow cannot be translated to one fixed severity without reading the warning content and matrix.

sources.name: Amber-warning interpretation
verified_claims: Amber indicates increased likelihood of severe-weather impacts including possible travel disruption, closures, power cuts and risk to life or property.
limitations: The listed impacts are possibilities across the warning area and not confirmed outcomes at every location.

sources.name: Four warning-impact levels
verified_claims: Warning impact levels are very low, low, medium and high.
limitations: Impact level is categorical and should not be used as a parcel loss estimate.

sources.name: Within-area impact variability
verified_claims: Not every location in a warning area will necessarily experience the same impact level.
limitations: Area coverage must not be spatially joined as uniform parcel exposure.

sources.name: Prior-condition impact dependency
verified_claims: Previous weather conditions can change impacts, such as saturated ground increasing flooding from modest rainfall.
limitations: A hazard threshold must not be interpreted without antecedent-condition context.

sources.name: Nested lower-impact expectation
verified_claims: When severe impacts are expected, impacts at lower levels are also likely.
limitations: Nested impacts do not justify double-counting the same event across severity categories.

sources.name: Warning colour-alone guard
verified_claims: Users are instructed to read the warning details and matrix rather than rely on colour alone.
limitations: Any automated candidate must retain headline, impact, likelihood and geographic context.
